title: Benchmark Results Chart
description: Three implementations charted under mean-with-error-bars and best-of-N on a shared axis, with a callout explaining what each statistic conceals.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Benchmarking
Statistics

learningObjectives: Choose a statistic appropriate to a real-time requirement

controls.label: Any bar
controls.purpose: Exact value, std dev, and implied range

simulationModel.modelType: Fixed benchmark dataset under two summary statistics
equations: error bar extent = mean ± 1 standard deviation
assumptions: Shared y-axis range across both views
limitations: Shows two statistics; percentile-based reporting such as p99 is often better for real-time work and is not shown

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Same data, two summaries, with the ranking deliberately unchanged
keyQuestions: Does the ranking change between statistics?
Which implementation would you ship against a 440 microsecond deadline?
commonMisconceptions: That the lowest mean is the best choice
assessmentOpportunities: Identify what a best-of-N-only report conceals
